edges.reason: The target explicitly includes the multiplication-division relation, so multiplication meaning is needed for that inverse-operation assertion.

Two-digit integer division prepares legitimate two-digit-divisor cases. The stated criterion also permits a one-digit divisor, and the decimal-place extension can be learned from that simpler algorithm, so the entire two-digit trial-quotient method is not universal.

The target explicitly computes a one-place decimal divided by an integer and writes a decimal result; decimal-by-decimal multiplication is an unrelated procedure. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
edges.scope: Decimal place and value meanings when dividing a decimal dividend and writing a decimal quotient

edges.reason: An equal-part refinement diagram establishes fraction equivalence without a quotient-invariance proof. The division interpretation is useful preparation or an optional proof route.
edges.scope: justifying the property through fraction as division

edges.reason: The assertion that the fraction's value stays unchanged requires interpreting the fraction's represented quantity.

The criteria expressly find common factors and reduce until numerator and denominator are coprime. These are the common-factor contents of the endpoint; finding the greatest factor in a single step is only a shortcut and is outside this required scope.
edges.scope: Finding a shared divisor and recognizing the absence of a shared divisor above one when reducing to simplest form

edges.reason: Reduction replaces numerator and denominator by division by the same common factor, using the value-preserving fraction property.
edges.scope: dividing numerator and denominator by a common number

edges.reason: The correspondence to decimal places uses tenths and hundredths decimal place-value meanings directly.
edges.scope: decimal place value as tenths and hundredths

edges.reason: Writing a tenths/hundredths fraction as a decimal uses the numerator and equal-part-size meanings of that fraction.
